thread:
Alex M: FYI customer on private VPC (acme-corp) reporting spikes of 429s and a billing jump overnight. They run a per-pod sidecar limiter + nginx-ingress. logs attached.
Maria S: Can you paste the minimal nginx + sidecar config and a short repro? Want to confirm if it's ingress or sidecar backpressure.
Jordan R: Quick paste of what they're using:
```
# nginx-ingress fragment
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=req_zone:10m rate=20r/s;
limit_req zone=req_zone burst=100 nodelay;

# sidecar (envoy) local_rate_limit config snippet
local_rate_limit:
  token_bucket:
    max_tokens: 100
    fill_interval: 1s
    tokens_per_fill: 100
```
They also set the gateway to 100 concurrent connections per upstream.
Maria S: OK — a few red flags: nginx burst=100 + env token_bucket 100 with nodelay will accept big bursts and then immediately forward many requests to the gateway, which can exhaust the dedicated capacity and trigger 429s upstream. Also billing spike makes sense: retries + bursts -> extra tokens.
Alex M: Customer says the pattern is: short traffic burst from a scheduled job (100 reqs/second for ~30s) -> 429s from gateway -> clients retry aggressively.
Jordan R: Repro steps I used locally:
1) curl loop from 10 threads: for i in {1..300}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private.acme/api & done
2) Observe nginx access logs show initial accept then 429s from upstream
3) Check sidecar admin: token_bucket tokens drop to 0 then refill slowly

IngressBot: Runbook: https://internal/runs/playbooks/sidecar-ratecap
Maria S: Suggested fixes to propose to customer:
- Reduce nginx burst to something closer to expected burst (eg burst=20) so ingress smooths bursts instead of passing them wholesale.
- Change envoy token_bucket to smaller max_tokens and enable "smoothing" (fill_interval=250ms, tokens_per_fill=25) to spread bursts.
- On gateway side, enable per-customer leaky bucket with short splay (randomized refill jitter) and a Retry-After header to clients.
- Add client-side exponential backoff & jitter to scheduled job.
- If they need burst absorption, use a short-lived queue/buffer layer (redis/ingress buffer) instead of huge token buckets in the sidecar.
Alex M: Also warned customer about billing: retries into hosted endpoints count tokens. Recommend rate-limited fallbacks or lower-quality cheaper model for bursts.
Jordan R: Quick config diff to recommend:
```
# nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=req_zone:10m rate=20r/s;
limit_req zone=req_zone burst=20 nodelay;

# envoy token bucket -> smoothing
token_bucket:
  max_tokens: 40
  fill_interval: 250ms
  tokens_per_fill: 10
```
Maria S: I'm going to send these as a support note and propose a short canary change for 24h. I'll include sample curl repro and suggested k8s manifest edits. :thumbsup:
Alex M: Thanks — mark as escalated to SRE for gateway-side leaky bucket tuning if nginx/sidecar changes don't fully resolve.
IngressBot: Note: created incident link INC-2314 and attached logs from the gateway."
